functions.name: VW::get_stride

functions.name: VW::init_features

functions.name: VW::set_feature

functions.name: VW_InitializeA
functions.signature: VW_HANDLE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_InitializeA(const char* pstrArgs)
functions.description: C API. Initializes a VW instance from an ANSI argument string. Returns an opaque VW_HANDLE.
requirements: pstrArgs must be a null-terminated string of valid VW arguments
Returned handle must be released via VW_Finish when no longer needed

functions.name: VW_InitializeEscapedA
functions.signature: VW_HANDLE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_InitializeEscapedA(const char* pstrArgs)
functions.description: C API. Initializes a VW instance from an ANSI argument string with backslash-escaped spaces. Returns VW_HANDLE.
requirements: pstrArgs must be a null-terminated escaped argument string
Returned handle must be released via VW_Finish

functions.name: VW_InitializeWithModel
functions.signature: VW_HANDLE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_InitializeWithModel(const char* pstrArgs, const char* modelData, size_t modelDataSize)
functions.description: C API. Initializes a VW instance from arguments and an in-memory model blob.
requirements: pstrArgs must be a null-terminated VW argument string
modelData must point to model bytes of length modelDataSize (if non-zero) valid for the configured VW version
Returned handle must be released via VW_Finish

functions.name: VW_InitializeWithModelEscaped
functions.signature: VW_HANDLE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_InitializeWithModelEscaped(const char* pstrArgs, const char* modelData, size_t modelDataSize)
functions.description: C API. Initializes a VW instance from escaped arguments and an in-memory model blob.
requirements: pstrArgs must be a null-terminated escaped VW argument string
modelData must point to model bytes of length modelDataSize (if non-zero)
Returned handle must be released via VW_Finish

functions.name: VW_SeedWithModel
functions.signature: VW_HANDLE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_SeedWithModel(VW_HANDLE handle, const char* extraArgs)
functions.description: C API. Creates a new VW instance seeded from an existing one, sharing model weights, applying extraArgs. Use with caution; not all reductions are safe when seeded.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE from VW_Initialize*
extraArgs must be a null-terminated VW argument string compatible with the base handle
Returned handle must be released via VW_Finish

functions.name: VW_Finish_Passes
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_Finish_Passes(VW_HANDLE handle)
functions.description: C API. Finalizes learning passes (driver finalization tasks).
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE

functions.name: VW_Finish
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_Finish(VW_HANDLE handle)
functions.description: C API. Cleans up and frees a VW instance created by VW_Initialize*.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE created by VW_Initialize* or VW_SeedWithModel
Must be called exactly once per handle

functions.name: VW_ImportExample
functions.signature: VW_EXAMPLE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_ImportExample(VW_HANDLE handle, const char* label, VW_FEATURE_SPACE features, size_t len)
functions.description: C API. Builds an example from a label string and a feature space array.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
features must be a VW_FEATURE_SPACE obtained from VW_InitializeFeatureSpaces and filled via VW_InitFeatures/VW_SetFeature
len must match the number of feature spaces provided
Returned VW_EXAMPLE must eventually be finished via VW_FinishExample

functions.name: VW_InitializeFeatureSpaces
functions.signature: VW_FEATURE_SPACE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_InitializeFeatureSpaces(size_t len)
functions.description: C API. Allocates an array of feature spaces of length len for constructing examples programmatically.
requirements: len is the number of feature spaces to allocate
Caller must later release via VW_ReleaseFeatureSpace when used with VW_ExportExample or appropriate free path for constructor helpers

functions.name: VW_GetFeatureSpace
functions.signature: VW_FEATURE_SPACE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetFeatureSpace(VW_FEATURE_SPACE first, size_t index)
functions.description: C API. Returns a handle to a specific feature space entry within the allocated array.
requirements: first must be a valid VW_FEATURE_SPACE returned by VW_InitializeFeatureSpaces
index must be within [0, len) of the allocated array

functions.name: VW_ExportExample
functions.signature: VW_FEATURE_SPACE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_ExportExample(VW_HANDLE handle, VW_EXAMPLE e, size_t* plen)
functions.description: C API. Exports an example’s features into an allocated feature space array and writes its length to plen. Must be freed with VW_ReleaseFeatureSpace.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE from the same handle
plen must be non-null and writable
Caller must call VW_ReleaseFeatureSpace on the returned feature space with the provided length

functions.name: VW_ReleaseFeatureSpace
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_ReleaseFeatureSpace(VW_FEATURE_SPACE features, size_t len)
functions.description: C API. Frees a feature space array allocated by VW_ExportExample.
requirements: features must be a VW_FEATURE_SPACE previously returned by VW_ExportExample
len must match the length returned by VW_ExportExample

functions.name: VW_ReadExampleA
functions.signature: VW_EXAMPLE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_ReadExampleA(VW_HANDLE handle, const char* line)
functions.description: C API. Parses a VW-format example line into an example.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
line must be a null-terminated VW-format string
Returned VW_EXAMPLE must be finished via VW_FinishExample

functions.name: VW_StartParser
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_StartParser(VW_HANDLE handle)
functions.description: C API. Starts the parser for the given handle.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
Must be paired with VW_EndParser

functions.name: VW_EndParser
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_EndParser(VW_HANDLE handle)
functions.description: C API. Stops the parser for the given handle.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
Should be called after VW_StartParser

functions.name: VW_GetExample
functions.signature: VW_EXAMPLE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetExample(VW_HANDLE handle)
functions.description: C API. Retrieves the next available example from the parser.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
Returned VW_EXAMPLE must be finished via VW_FinishExample

functions.name: VW_FinishExample
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_FinishExample(VW_HANDLE handle, VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Signals that an example is finished and may be recycled or freed.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE obtained from this handle
Must be called exactly once per example lifecycle

functions.name: VW_GetLabel
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetLabel(VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Returns the example’s scalar label value (if any).
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE with a scalar label

functions.name: VW_GetImportance
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetImportance(VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Returns the example’s importance (weight).
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE

functions.name: VW_GetInitial
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetInitial(VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Returns the example’s initial prediction/base value.
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE

functions.name: VW_GetPrediction
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetPrediction(VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Returns the example’s scalar prediction.
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE

functions.name: VW_GetCostSensitivePrediction
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetCostSensitivePrediction(VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Returns the example’s cost-sensitive prediction as a scalar.
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE configured for cost-sensitive prediction

functions.name: VW_GetMultilabelPredictions
functions.signature: void* VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetMultilabelPredictions(VW_EXAMPLE e, size_t* plen)
functions.description: C API. Returns a pointer to the multilabel predictions array and writes its length to plen. Pointer is owned by the example.
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE with multilabel predictions available
plen must be non-null and writable
Do not free or use the returned pointer after the example is finished

functions.name: VW_GetTopicPrediction
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetTopicPrediction(VW_EXAMPLE e, size_t i)
functions.description: C API. Returns the topic prediction at index i. i ranges from 0 to max topic - 1.
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE
i must be within the topic prediction array bounds

functions.name: VW_GetActionScore
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetActionScore(VW_EXAMPLE e, size_t i)
functions.description: C API. Returns the action score at index i.
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE
i must be within bounds of the action score array

functions.name: VW_GetActionScoreLength
functions.signature: size_t VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetActionScoreLength(VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Returns the number of action scores for the example.
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE

functions.name: VW_GetCatsActionPdfValuePrediction
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetCatsActionPdfValuePrediction(VW_EXAMPLE example, float action_and_pdf_value[2])
functions.description: C API. For CATS, writes the chosen action and its PDF value into the provided 2-element array.
requirements: example must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE with a CATS prediction available
action_and_pdf_value must point to an array of at least 2 floats

functions.name: VW_GetTagLength
functions.signature: size_t VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetTagLength(VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Returns the length of the example’s tag.
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE

functions.name: VW_GetTag
functions.signature: const char* VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetTag(VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Returns a pointer to the example’s tag data (not null-terminated).
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE
Returned pointer is owned by the example; do not free and do not use after the example is finished

functions.name: VW_GetFeatureNumber
functions.signature: size_t VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetFeatureNumber(VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Returns the number of features on the example.
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE

functions.name: VW_GetConfidence
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetConfidence(VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Returns the prediction confidence for the example, if available.
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE

functions.name: VW_SetFeatureSpace
functions.signature: size_t VW_CALLING_CONV VW_SetFeatureSpace(VW_HANDLE handle, VW_FEATURE_SPACE feature_space, const char* name)
functions.description: C API. Sets the namespace name for a feature space entry and associates it with the handle for example construction. Returns an index or size (exact semantics not documented).
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
feature_space must be a valid feature space entry from VW_InitializeFeatureSpaces
name must be a null-terminated namespace name string

functions.name: VW_InitFeatures
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_InitFeatures(VW_FEATURE_SPACE feature_space, size_t features_count)
functions.description: C API. Allocates and initializes the feature array inside a feature space to the specified count.
requirements: feature_space must be a valid VW_FEATURE_SPACE entry
features_count is the number of features to allocate for this namespace

functions.name: VW_GetFeature
functions.signature: VW_FEATURE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetFeature(VW_FEATURE_SPACE feature_space, size_t index)
functions.description: C API. Returns a handle to a specific feature entry within a feature space.
requirements: feature_space must be a valid VW_FEATURE_SPACE
index must be within the allocated features_count

functions.name: VW_SetFeature
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_SetFeature(VW_FEATURE feature, size_t index, size_t feature_hash, float value)
functions.description: C API. Sets a feature’s hashed index and value at the given position for the given feature handle.
requirements: feature must be a valid VW_FEATURE obtained from VW_GetFeature
index must be within the allocated features_count for that feature space

functions.name: VW_GetFeatures
functions.signature: VW_FEATURE VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetFeatures(VW_HANDLE handle, VW_EXAMPLE e, size_t* plen)
functions.description: C API. Returns a pointer to the example’s raw features and writes the number of features to plen. Must return via VW_ReturnFeatures.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE from this handle
plen must be non-null and writable
Caller must call VW_ReturnFeatures with the returned VW_FEATURE when done

functions.name: VW_ReturnFeatures
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_ReturnFeatures(VW_FEATURE f)
functions.description: C API. Returns a feature array obtained from VW_GetFeatures back to VW.
requirements: f must be a VW_FEATURE previously returned by VW_GetFeatures and not already returned

functions.name: VW_HashSpaceA
functions.signature: size_t VW_CALLING_CONV VW_HashSpaceA(VW_HANDLE handle, const char* s)
functions.description: C API. Hashes a namespace string using the handle’s hasher and seed.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
s must be a null-terminated string

functions.name: VW_HashSpaceStaticA
functions.signature: size_t VW_CALLING_CONV VW_HashSpaceStaticA(const char* s, const char* h)
functions.description: C API. Hashes a namespace string using a named static hasher and seed 0.
requirements: s and h must be null-terminated strings
h must name a supported hasher

functions.name: VW_HashFeatureA
functions.signature: size_t VW_CALLING_CONV VW_HashFeatureA(VW_HANDLE handle, const char* s, size_t u)
functions.description: C API. Hashes a feature name using seed u and the handle’s hasher/mask.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
s must be a null-terminated string

functions.name: VW_HashFeatureStaticA
functions.signature: size_t VW_CALLING_CONV VW_HashFeatureStaticA(const char* s, size_t u, const char* h, unsigned int num_bits)
functions.description: C API. Hashes a feature name using hasher h, seed u, and masks to num_bits.
requirements: s and h must be null-terminated strings
h must name a supported hasher
num_bits must be within a reasonable range for hashing/masking

functions.name: VW_Learn
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_Learn(VW_HANDLE handle, VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Learns on the given example (updates the model) and returns the prediction.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE configured for learning
e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE from this handle
Example should be properly set up before learning and finished afterwards via VW_FinishExample

functions.name: VW_Predict
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_Predict(VW_HANDLE handle, VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Predicts on the given example without updating the model; returns the prediction.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE from this handle

functions.name: VW_PredictCostSensitive
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_PredictCostSensitive(VW_HANDLE handle, VW_EXAMPLE e)
functions.description: C API. Produces a cost-sensitive prediction for the example and returns it as a scalar.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE configured for cost-sensitive prediction

functions.name: VW_AddLabel
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_AddLabel(VW_EXAMPLE e, float label, float weight, float base)
functions.description: C API. Deprecated. Sets label, weight, and base on an example. Prefer passing labels via VW_ReadExample/VW_ImportExample.
requirements: e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE
weight should be non-negative (typical semantics)

functions.name: VW_AddStringLabel
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_AddStringLabel(VW_HANDLE handle, VW_EXAMPLE e, const char* label)
functions.description: C API. Deprecated. Parses and assigns a label string to an example using the handle’s label parser.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
e must be a valid VW_EXAMPLE
label must be a null-terminated label string valid for the configured learner

functions.name: VW_Get_Weight
functions.signature: float VW_CALLING_CONV VW_Get_Weight(VW_HANDLE handle, size_t index, size_t offset)
functions.description: C API. Reads a weight value from the model’s weight vector at (index << stride_shift) + offset.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
index and offset must be within the allocated weights range

functions.name: VW_Set_Weight
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_Set_Weight(VW_HANDLE handle, size_t index, size_t offset, float value)
functions.description: C API. Writes a weight value into the model’s weight vector at (index << stride_shift) + offset.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
index and offset must be within the allocated weights range

functions.name: VW_Num_Weights
functions.signature: size_t VW_CALLING_CONV VW_Num_Weights(VW_HANDLE handle)
functions.description: C API. Returns the number of weight indices in the model.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE

functions.name: VW_Get_Stride
functions.signature: size_t VW_CALLING_CONV VW_Get_Stride(VW_HANDLE handle)
functions.description: C API. Returns the stride (weights per index) used by the model.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE

functions.name: VW_SaveModel
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_SaveModel(VW_HANDLE handle)
functions.description: C API. Saves the model according to the handle’s configured output settings (e.g., -f).
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
Handle must have been configured with appropriate save parameters to persist the model

functions.name: VW_CopyModelData
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_CopyModelData(VW_HANDLE handle, VW_IOBUF* bufferHandle, char** outputData, size_t* outputSize)
functions.description: C API. Copies the model into an internal buffer and returns a pointer/size to the data. The buffer is referenced by bufferHandle and must be freed with VW_FreeIOBuf.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
bufferHandle, outputData, and outputSize must be non-null pointers to receive outputs
Caller must call VW_FreeIOBuf with the returned bufferHandle to free the buffer

functions.name: VW_FreeIOBuf
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_FreeIOBuf(VW_IOBUF bufferHandle)
functions.description: C API. Frees an IO buffer previously returned by VW_CopyModelData.
requirements: bufferHandle must be a valid VW_IOBUF obtained from VW_CopyModelData and not already freed

functions.name: VW_CaptureAuditData
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_CaptureAuditData(VW_HANDLE handle)
functions.description: C API. Enables capturing audit data during learning/prediction.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE

functions.name: VW_ClearCapturedAuditData
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_ClearCapturedAuditData(VW_HANDLE handle)
functions.description: C API. Disables and clears captured audit data.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE

functions.name: VW_GetAuditDataA
functions.signature: char* VW_CALLING_CONV VW_GetAuditDataA(VW_HANDLE handle, size_t* size)
functions.description: C API. Retrieves captured audit data as an ANSI char buffer and writes its size. Caller must free via VW_FreeAuditDataA.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
size must be non-null and writable
Caller must free the returned buffer using VW_FreeAuditDataA(handle, data)

functions.name: VW_FreeAuditDataA
functions.signature: void VW_CALLING_CONV VW_FreeAuditDataA(VW_HANDLE handle, char* data)
functions.description: C API. Frees a buffer returned by VW_GetAuditDataA.
requirements: handle must be a valid VW_HANDLE
data must be a pointer previously returned by VW_GetAuditDataA for this handle and not already freed

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for VW command-line arguments strings
# Goal: produce valid/interesting VW arg lines covering diverse modes
# Constraints: return bytes <= 4096, deterministic w.r.t seed

_LOSSES = [
    "squared", "logistic", "hinge", "quantile", "poisson", "cross_entropy"
]

_LINKS = ["identity", "logistic"]

_HASHERS = ["strings", "all"]

_REDUCTIONS = [
    # Common supervised
    ("--oaa", lambda r: str(r.randint(2, 10))),
    ("--multilabel_oaa", lambda r: str(r.randint(2, 8))),
    ("--csoaa", lambda r: str(r.randint(2, 8))),
    # Contextual bandit variants (single-line when possible)
    ("--cb_explore_adf", None),
    ("--ccb_explore_adf", None),
]

_BOOL_FLAGS = [
    "--audit", "--invert_hash", "--holdout_off", "--quiet", "--keep_best_constants",
    "--preserve_performance_counters", "--json", "--binary"
]

# Namespace and feature interactions
def _gen_interactions(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tokens = []
    # Letters represent namespaces in VW text; include interactions to affect feature config
    letters = "abcxyz"[: r.randint(2, 6)]
    # -q pairwise interactions
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)):
        a, b = r.choice(letters), r.choice(letters)
        tokens += ["-q", f"{a}{b}"]
    # --interactions higher-order
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        k = r.randint(3, 4)
        s = ''.join(r.choice(letters) for _ in range(k))
        tokens += ["--interactions", s]
    return tokens

# Learning rate schedule and optimization
def _gen_optim(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tokens = []
    lr = 10 ** r.uniform(-3.5, 0.2)
    tokens += ["-l", f"{lr:.6g}"]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        power_t = r.uniform(0.0, 0.8)
        tokens += ["--power_t", f"{power_t:.3f}"]
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        tokens += ["--l2", f"{10 ** r.uniform(-8, -2):.3g}"]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        tokens += ["--l1", f"{10 ** r.uniform(-8, -2):.3g}"]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        tokens += ["--decay_learning_rate", f"{r.uniform(0.0, 1.0):.3f}"]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        tokens += ["--adaptive"]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        tokens += ["--invariant"]
    return tokens

# Model size / hashing settings
def _gen_hashing(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tokens = []
    num_bits = r.choice([16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 25])
    tokens += ["-b", str(num_bits)]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        tokens += ["--hash", r.choice(_HASHERS)]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        tokens += ["--ngram", str(r.randint(1, 3))]
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        tokens += ["--skips", str(r.randint(0, 2))]
    return tokens

# Loss / link / passes / cache
def _gen_general(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tokens = []
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        tokens += ["--loss_function", r.choice(_LOSSES)]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        tokens += ["--link", r.choice(_LINKS)]
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        passes_ = r.randint(1, 5)
        tokens += ["--passes", str(passes_)]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        tokens += ["--holdout_off"]
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        tokens += ["--early_terminate", str(r.randint(1, 3))]
    # Cache settings: generate a cache file name but not actually used by fuzzer
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        fname = _rand_filename(r, ext=".cache")
        tokens += ["--cache_file", fname]
    return tokens

# Output-related flags that are path-like but safe strings
def _gen_outputs(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tokens = []
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        tokens += ["-f", _rand_filename(r, ".vw")]
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        tokens += ["--readable_model", _rand_filename(r, ".readable")]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        tokens += ["--predictions", _rand_filename(r, ".pred")]
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        tokens += ["--raw_predictions", _rand_filename(r, ".raw")]
    return tokens

def _rand_filename(r: random.Random, ext: str = "") -> str:
    base = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_") for _ in range(r.randint(4, 12)))
    return base + ext

def _gen_bool_flags(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    flags = []
    picks = r.sample(_BOOL_FLAGS, k=r.randint(0, min(4, len(_BOOL_FLAGS))))
    flags.extend(picks)
    return flags

def _gen_reduction(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    flag, valfun = r.choice(_REDUCTIONS)
    if valfun is None:
        return [flag]
    else:
        return [flag, valfun(r)]

def _gen_dictionary(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tokens = []
    # Namespace default interactions and ignore
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        ns = ''.join(r.sample(list(string.ascii_lowercase), k=r.randint(1, 3)))
        tokens += ["--ignore", ns]
    # Keep/affix hash
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        tokens += ["--affix", "+1*2"]
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        tokens += ["--spelling", str(r.randint(1, 2))]
    return tokens

def _mix_args(parts: List[List[str]], r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Flatten and shuffle groups to vary ordering while keeping flag-value adjacency
    seqs = [p[:] for p in parts if p]
    r.shuffle(seqs)
    flat: List[str] = []
    for s in seqs:
        flat.extend(s)
    return flat

def _ensure_minimal_valid(tokens: List[str], r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Ensure at least one reduction/learner is specified to change feature compatibility
    has_any = any(t in {"--oaa", "--multilabel_oaa", "--csoaa", "--cb_explore_adf", "--ccb_explore_adf"} for t in tokens)
    if not has_any:
        tokens = tokens + _gen_reduction(r)
    # Always include a benign quiet sometimes to reduce noise
    if "--quiet" not in tokens and r.random() < 0.5:
        tokens.append("--quiet")
    return tokens

def _build_cmd(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    parts.append(_gen_reduction(r))
    parts.append(_gen_interactions(r))
    parts.append(_gen_optim(r))
    parts.append(_gen_hashing(r))
    parts.append(_gen_general(r))
    parts.append(_gen_outputs(r))
    parts.append(_gen_bool_flags(r))
    parts.append(_gen_dictionary(r))

    tokens = _mix_args(parts, r)
    tokens = _ensure_minimal_valid(tokens, r)

    # Positional data source example: not needed for parser creation; omit to avoid file IO.
    # Join ensuring proper spacing, no quotes required for our character set.
    cmd = " ".join(tokens)
    return cmd

# Public entry point

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Generate 1-3 separate command lines concatenated with newline so multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls get varied inputs
    cmds = []
    n = r.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(n):
        cmd = _build_cmd(r)
        cmds.append(cmd)
    blob = "\n".join(cmds)
    # Truncate to budget
    b = blob.encode("utf-8")[:4096]
    return b

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator focuses on producing valid VW label strings for various common
# reductions/parsers so VW::parse_example_label can successfully parse them.
# It mixes among several families:
# - Simple scalar/regression/classification labels
# - Weighted labels (label weight base)
# - Cost-sensitive (single and multiclass with costs)
# - Contextual bandit (CB) and CB ADF style labels
# - Multilabel
# - CCB (conditional contextual bandit) action/shared lines
# The fuzzer stub only requests FUZZ_PARAM_STR once, so we return a single
# interesting label string per call.

_NUMERIC = [
    "0", "1", "-1", "0.0", "1.0", "-1.0", "0.5", "2.5", "10", "-3.25",
]

# Helpers for distributions

def _rand_float(r: random.Random, a: float = -5.0, b: float = 5.0) -> str:
    # Avoid NaN/inf, keep reasonable precision
    return f"{r.uniform(a, b):.6g}"


def _rand_pos_float(r: random.Random, a: float = 0.0, b: float = 5.0) -> str:
    # importance/weight should be non-negative; keep some zeros too
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        return "0"
    return f"{max(a, r.random() * (b - a) + a):.6g}"


def _rand_uint(r: random.Random, lo: int = 1, hi: int = 10) -> str:
    return str(r.randint(lo, hi))


# Label constructors

def make_simple_scalar(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Simple label (regression or binary) possibly with weight and base
    base = r.choice(_NUMERIC + [_rand_float(r)])
    parts = [base]
    # Optionally add weight and initial prediction/base
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        weight = _rand_pos_float(r)
        parts.append(weight)
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            init = _rand_float(r)
            parts.append(init)
    # Optional tag
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        parts.append("'tag")
    return " ".join(parts)


def make_multiclass(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Multiclass label is an integer class id, optionally with weight and base
    cls = _rand_uint(r, 1, 10)
    parts = [cls]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(_rand_pos_float(r))
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(_rand_float(r))
    return " ".join(parts)


def make_cost_sensitive(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Cost-sensitive supports space-separated class:cost pairs, optional weight
    k = r.randint(1, 5)
    pairs = []
    used = set()
    for _ in range(k):
        c = r.randint(1, 10)
        if c in used:
            continue
        used.add(c)
        cost = _rand_float(r, -1.0, 5.0)
        pairs.append(f"{c}:{cost}")
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        pairs.append(_rand_pos_float(r))  # example level weight
    return " ".join(pairs)


def make_multilabel(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Multilabel expects space separated integers inside labels for multilabel task
    # In VW text, multilabel often uses space separated ints; a common explicit
    # form is: "1,2,3" or "1 2 3" depending on parser. We prefer space form.
    n = r.randint(1, 6)
    labels = sorted(set(r.randint(1, 15) for _ in range(n)))
    return " ".join(str(x) for x in labels)


def make_cb(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Contextual Bandit label: action:cost:probability optionally multiple for exploration data
    # Form: "a:c:p" or multiple "a1:c1:p1 a2:c2:p2"; ensure 0<p<=1
    m = r.randint(1, 3)
    entries = []
    used = set()
    for _ in range(m):
        a = r.randint(1, 10)
        if a in used and r.random() < 0.7:
            continue
        used.add(a)
        c = _rand_float(r, -1.0, 5.0)
        p = f"{max(1e-6, min(1.0, r.random())):.6g}"
        entries.append(f"{a}:{c}:{p}")
    return " ".join(entries)


def make_cb_adf_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # ADF uses separate example lines, but parse_example_label may accept per-line labels
    # Common ADF per-line labels:
    # - shared: "shared"
    # - action-only: ""
    # - chosen action feedback: "a:c:p"
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        return "shared"
    elif choice < 0.5:
        # partial feedback for single action
        a = r.randint(1, 10)
        c = _rand_float(r, -1.0, 5.0)
        p = f"{max(1e-6, min(1.0, r.random())):.6g}"
        return f"{a}:{c}:{p}"
    else:
        # empty or weight-only allowed in some contexts; keep simple to stay valid
        return make_simple_scalar(r)


def make_ccb(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # CCB can have labels like:
    # - shared (treated specially)
    # - action
    # - slot with outcome: e.g., "ccb slot 1:0.5:0.2,3:0.0:0.8"
    # For safety, provide simpler forms commonly accepted by parser:
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        return "ccb shared"
    elif r.random() < 0.8:
        return "ccb action"
    else:
        # slot with one or two outcomes: a:cost:prob
        k = r.randint(1, 2)
        outs = []
        used = set()
        for _ in range(k):
            a = r.randint(1, 10)
            if a in used:
                continue
            used.add(a)
            c = _rand_float(r, -1.0, 5.0)
            p = f"{max(1e-6, min(1.0, r.random())):.6g}"
            outs.append(f"{a}:{c}:{p}")
        return "ccb slot " + ",".join(outs)


def make_slates(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Slates labels could be: "slates shared", "slates action 1", "slates slot 0.1"
    t = r.random()
    if t < 0.33:
        return "slates shared"
    elif t < 0.66:
        return f"slates action {r.randint(1,10)}"
    else:
        return f"slates slot {_rand_float(r, 0.0, 1.0)}"


def make_topic(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # LDA/topic models often use unlabeled examples; provide weight/base only
    # e.g., "|f ..." would be features, but label parser often sees empty.
    # Use weight/base style so it parses as label fields even without explicit label.
    w = _rand_pos_float(r)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return w
    else:
        return f"{w} {_rand_float(r)}"


_BUILDERS = [
    make_simple_scalar,
    make_multiclass,
    make_cost_sensitive,
    make_multilabel,
    make_cb,
    make_cb_adf_like,
    make_ccb,
    make_slates,
    make_topic,
]


def _choose_builder(r: random.Random):
    # Bias toward the most common labels (simple, multiclass, CS, CB)
    weights = [
        0.20,  # simple
        0.15,  # multiclass
        0.15,  # cost sensitive
        0.08,  # multilabel
        0.18,  # cb
        0.10,  # cb adf-like
        0.07,  # ccb
        0.04,  # slates
        0.03,  # topic-ish
    ]
    x = r.random()
    acc = 0.0
    for b, w in zip(_BUILDERS, weights):
        acc += w
        if x <= acc:
            return b
    return _BUILDERS[-1]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Occasionally force specific edge cases likely to tick different code paths
    special_cases = [
        "",  # empty label (often valid for prediction-only paths)
        "nan",  # sometimes parsed as string, but keep rare
        "Inf",  # unlikely, keep rare
        "shared",  # common keyword for CB ADF
        "ccb shared",
    ]
    if r.random() < 0.08:
        s = r.choice(special_cases)
        return s.encode("utf-8")

    builder = _choose_builder(r)
    s = builder(r)

    # Ensure non-empty, fall back to simple scalar if needed
    if not s:
        s = make_simple_scalar(r)

    # Trim and cap length conservatively
    s = s.strip()
    if len(s) > 4000:
        s = s[:4000]
    return s.encode("utf-8")

import os
import random
import secrets
from typing import List

# Generator for filesystem path strings suitable for writing a model file.
# The target stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to obtain a writable path in a temp area.
# Our job is to return bytes that the harness will use as the file content behind that filename
# or, depending on the harness, as the initial bytes that seed FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME().
# Since FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME expects a path, we craft a plausible, writable relative path.
# We keep it portable and within 4096 bytes.

_SAFE_CHARS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789._-"

def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(_SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))

def _choose_extension(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common VW model extensions or generic binary/text
    exts = [
        "model", "vw", "bin", "txt", "gz", "zst", "lz4", "", "mdl"
    ]
    ext = rng.choice(exts)
    return ("." + ext) if ext else ""

def _make_components(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    comps: List[str] = []
    # sometimes create nested directories
    depth = rng.choices([0,1,2,3], weights=[2,3,3,1])[0]
    for _ in range(depth):
        d = _rand_name(rng, 1, rng.randint(3, 10))
        # occasionally add a dot-folder or dash
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            d = "." + d
        comps.append(d)
    # filename
    base = _rand_name(rng, 3, rng.randint(5, 18))
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        # include multiple dots to exercise path parsing
        base = base + "." + _rand_name(rng, 2, 5)
    base += _choose_extension(rng)
    comps.append(base)
    return comps

def _maybe_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Return a prefix to vary relative/absolute/temp-like paths
    choices = []
    # Prefer relative paths to remain writable in typical harness temp dirs
    choices.append("")
    choices.append("./")
    # Occasionally attempt sub-temp directories
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        choices.append("tmp/")
        choices.append("build/")
    # Rare absolute-like Unix path (some harnesses remap to temp). Use /tmp to increase writability.
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        choices.append("/tmp/")
    # Very rare Windows-like relative
    if rng.random() < 0.05:
        drive = chr(ord('C') + rng.randrange(0, 3))
        choices.append(f"{drive}:/temp/")
    return rng.choice(choices)

def _compose_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    prefix = _maybe_prefix(rng)
    comps = _make_components(rng)
    # Join with forward slashes to be broadly acceptable; Windows APIs typically accept them too.
    path = prefix + "/".join(filter(None, comps))
    # Ensure length bound
    if len(path) > 200:  # keep modest
        path = path[:200]
    return path

def _encode_path_to_bytes(path: str) -> bytes:
    # FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME expects a C-string; many harnesses accept bytes containing the path.
    # Provide UTF-8 bytes without null terminator; harness typically appends as needed.
    return path.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create a small corpus of interesting candidate paths and pick one per call for variability.
    candidates: List[str] = []

    # Straightforward relative file
    candidates.append(_compose_path(rng))

    # Hidden file in current dir
    candidates.append("./." + _rand_name(rng, 3, 10) + _choose_extension(rng))

    # Nested directories
    rng2 = random.Random(rng.randrange(1 << 30))
    candidates.append(_compose_path(rng2))

    # Temp-like names
    nonce = secrets.token_hex(4)
    candidates.append(f"./vw_model_{nonce}{_choose_extension(rng)}")

    # File without extension
    candidates.append("model_" + _rand_name(rng, 4, 8))

    # Dot extension variations
    candidates.append("./models/" + _rand_name(rng, 5, 9) + ".vw")
    candidates.append("./out/" + _rand_name(rng, 5, 9) + ".model")

    # Choose one path deterministically from candidates using RNG
    path = candidates[rng.randrange(len(candidates))]

    # Bound final size to 4096 bytes (way smaller here)
    data = _encode_path_to_bytes(path)
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Generate interesting valid arbitrary strings for VW hashing fuzzers.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used multiple times to supply namespace names, feature names,
# hasher names, and general strings. We therefore build a bytes payload that
# contains a sequence of NUL-terminated UTF-8 strings, covering:
# - typical ASCII tokens
# - unicode and emoji
# - strings with spaces, tabs, backslashes, quotes
# - very short and very long strings
# - strings resembling hasher names (e.g., murmur, crc, spooky, fnv)
# - strings with separators, punctuation, and edge chars
# The harness will read them sequentially; if it expects fewer, extra data is ignored.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

HASHER_LIKE = [
    "murmur", "murmurhash", "murmur2", "murmur3",
    "crc", "crc32", "crc64",
    "spooky", "spooky2",
    "fnv", "fnv1", "fnv1a",
    "xxhash", "cityhash",
    "siphash", "sha1", "sha256",
]

NAMESPACE_TOKENS = [
    "|ns", "|user", "|context", "|features", "|a", "|b", "|c",
    "namespace", "space", "feat", "abc", "xyz",
]

EDGE_STRINGS = [
    "",  # empty
    " ",  # single space
    "\t",  # tab
    "\\",  # backslash
    "\n",  # newline (as a content char)
    "\0",  # literal backslash-zero sequence in content
    "\u0000",  # literal escape text
    "\x00",  # literal
    "\"quoted\"",
    "'single'",
    "name=value",
    "feature:1.23",
    ":namespace:",
    "--option",
    "_",
    "-",
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "μhash", "naïve", "café", "пользователь", "用户",
    "日本語", "😀", "🚀✨", "mañana", "straße",
]

PUNCT = "!@#$%^&*()[]{};:,./?`~|\-=+""'"


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:" + PUNCT
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_unicode(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix of ascii + chosen unicode samples
    parts: List[str] = []
    target = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    while len("".join(parts)) < target:
        choice = r.randint(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append(r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES))
        elif choice == 1:
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 4))
        else:
            # pick a random BMP codepoint excluding surrogates
            cp = r.randint(0x20, 0xFFFF)
            if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                cp = 0x20
            parts.append(chr(cp))
    return "".join(parts)[:target]


def _interesting_strings(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []

    # Some fixed edge cases
    out.extend(EDGE_STRINGS)

    # Hasher-like names
    out.extend(HASHER_LIKE)

    # Namespace-like tokens (with/without pipes)
    out.extend(NAMESPACE_TOKENS)
    out.extend([t.replace("|", "") for t in NAMESPACE_TOKENS])

    # Feature-like patterns
    for k in ["color", "size", "price", "country", "device", "os", "browser"]:
        out.append(f"{k}")
        out.append(f"{k}=123")
        out.append(f"{k}:1.5")
        out.append(f"{k}_A-B/1")

    # Random ascii and unicode strings varying lengths
    for _ in range(20):
        out.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 8))
        out.append(_rand_ascii(r, 9, 24))
        out.append(_rand_unicode(r, 3, 16))

    # Long strings to exercise hashing on longer inputs
    out.append(_rand_ascii(r, 64, 128))
    out.append(_rand_unicode(r, 64, 128))

    # Strings with whitespace and escapes
    out.extend([
        "name with spaces",
        "tab\tseparated\tvalues",
        "backslash \\\ path \\server\\share",
        "quoted \"inner\" text",
        "pipe|separated|tokens",
        "comma,separated,values",
    ])

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for s in out:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            uniq.append(s)
    return uniq


def _pack_cstrings(strings: List[str], r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a blob of NUL-terminated UTF-8 strings in a randomized order
    r.shuffle(strings)

    blob = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        # Ensure we don't exceed size budget; keep room for final NUL
        if len(blob) + len(b) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        blob += b + b"\x00"

    # Ensure at least one string present
    if not blob:
        blob = bytearray(b"a\x00")
    return bytes(blob)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a pool of interesting strings
    strings = _interesting_strings(r)

    # Slightly bias to include some hasher names again to increase chance of selection
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        strings.append(r.choice(HASHER_LIKE))

    # Also include some numeric-looking strings which may be used as seeds in text
    for _ in range(5):
        strings.append(str(r.getrandbits(64)))

    # Finalize into a NUL-terminated string sequence
    return _pack_cstrings(strings, r)

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzzers that call:
# - VW::hash_space_static(s, h)
# - VW::hash_feature_static(s, u, h, num_bits)
# Both rely on valid hasher names (h) recognized by VW::get_hasher and arbitrary strings (s).
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR will read from this buffer sequentially to produce strings; thus we
# pack multiple interesting strings consecutively with length prefixes. We include:
# - a variety of valid hasher names
# - edge-case and typical feature/namespace strings (ASCII, unicode, long, empty)
# - seeds (u) and num_bits will be provided by the fuzzer via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned ...),
#   but we also include additional strings that may be consumed by multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
#
# Buffer format (self-descriptive, no external I/O):
# [u32 count]
#   repeated count times: [u32 len][len bytes]
# The fuzzer harness typically interprets FUZZ_PARAM_STR by pulling next slice; this format
# is common across these fuzzers.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

VALID_HASHERS = [
    b"all",            # common default
    b"murmur",         # murmur3
    b"murmur3",        # alias sometimes used
    b"spooky",         # spooky hash
    b"xxhash",         # xxhash
    b"xxhash64",       # variant
    b"crc",            # crc
    b"fnv",            # fnv
    b"sha1",           # some builds wire additional hashes
    b"md5",            # ditto
]

EDGE_STRINGS = [
    b"",                               # empty
    b" ",                              # single space
    b"feature",                        # simple ascii
    b"namespace",                      # simple ascii
    b"feat=value",                     # common pattern
    b"tab\tsep\tfield",                # tabs
    b"newline\nseparated",              # newline
    b"null\x00byte",                   # contains NUL inside
    "unicodé-✓-雪".encode("utf-8"),      # unicode
    b"A" * 1,                          # very short
    b"B" * 7,                          # small odd length
    b"C" * 31,                         # near small boundary
    b"D" * 255,                        # 255 bytes
    b"E" * 1024,                       # long
]

# Build a pool of candidate strings mixing valid hasher names and diverse payloads.

def _build_string_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    pool = []

    # Ensure multiple valid hasher names appear many times to increase selection probability.
    hashers = VALID_HASHERS.copy()
    rng.shuffle(hashers)
    for h in hashers:
        pool.append(h)
    # Add duplicates to bias towards valid names
    for _ in range(10):
        pool.append(rng.choice(VALID_HASHERS))

    # Add edge strings
    for s in EDGE_STRINGS:
        pool.append(s)

    # Add randomly composed strings combining tokens
    tokens = [b"user", b"session", b"id", b"click", b"ad", b"price", b"country", b"US", b"DE", b"CN", b"mobile", b"web"]
    for _ in range(20):
        parts = rng.choices(tokens, k=rng.randint(1, 5))
        sep = rng.choice([b"_", b"-", b":", b"=", b"/"])
        s = sep.join(parts)
        pool.append(s)

    # Add a few random-length binary-like strings (still bytes) to test arbitrary content
    for _ in range(10):
        ln = rng.randint(0, 128)
        s = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(ln))
        pool.append(s)

    return pool


def _pack_strings(strings: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Prefix with count, then each string as [u32 len][data]
    out = bytearray()
    out += struct.pack("<I", len(strings))
    for s in strings:
        out += struct.pack("<I", len(s))
        out += s
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    pool = _build_string_pool(rng)

    # Choose how many strings to emit. We need enough for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    # across both stubs; emitting 8-40 strings keeps within 4096 bytes.
    count = rng.randint(12, 40)

    # Ensure at least half of the entries are valid hasher names to satisfy h parameter.
    chosen: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Guaranteed valid hasher names
    needed_hashers = max(6, count // 2)
    for _ in range(needed_hashers):
        chosen.append(rng.choice(VALID_HASHERS))

    # 2) Add various feature/namespace strings
    while len(chosen) < count:
        chosen.append(rng.choice(pool))

    # 3) Shuffle to mix positions so either s or h may land on a valid hasher as required.
    rng.shuffle(chosen)

    # 4) Ensure first few positions are particularly useful: [feature-like, hasher, namespace-like, hasher]
    head = [
        b"user_id=42",
        rng.choice(VALID_HASHERS),
        b"price:9.99",
        rng.choice(VALID_HASHERS),
    ]
    # Replace the first entries with head for deterministic usefulness
    for i, v in enumerate(head):
        if i < len(chosen):
            chosen[i] = v
        else:
            chosen.append(v)

    buf = _pack_strings(chosen)

    # Truncate if somehow exceeded MAX_TOTAL (shouldn't normally). Ensure not to cut inside header; if too large, reduce count.
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Reduce strings until within limit
        while len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL and len(chosen) > 8:
            chosen.pop()  # remove last
            buf = _pack_strings(chosen)
        # As a last resort, hard truncate (still parseable if header matches); but keep header consistent
        if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
            # Repack with a smaller count
            trimmed = chosen[:8]
            buf = _pack_strings(trimmed)

    return buf
